summary: Post-upgrade quota refill latency causes transient 429s after organization credit increase
description:
Issue summary:
Customer upgraded org credit limit + billing tier (enterprise plan migration) at ~2026-03-09T23:00Z. Console shows new quota immediately, but customer observed a wave of 429 responses for short-lived streaming and bulk-embed jobs for ~8–12 minutes after upgrade.

Impact:
- SlateDocs reported ~15% of requests returning 429 during a 10-minute window affecting critical ingestion jobs (bulk embeddings + live chat).
- Customer reported degraded UX and 3 failed ingestion batches requiring manual retries.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (api and billing)
- Region: us-east-1
- Customer account: slate-12345
- Workloads: mixed low-latency streaming + periodic bulk embedding jobs

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Perform org credit/top-up via console (billing tier upgrade).
2) Immediately start parallel bulk-embed workers (100 concurrent sessions) and 50 concurrent short-lived streaming sessions.
3) Observe 429 rate and throttle headers on some calls for next 5–15 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows quota refreshed at 2026-03-09T23:00Z but rate-limiter logs indicate refill tokens were not applied uniformly to edge nodes for ~8 minutes.
- Throttle response headers (x-rw-rate-limit) show pre-upgrade limits consistent with the lower tier returned for some sessions.

Expected behavior:
- New quota should be available immediately across all serving nodes within the SLA window (<= 60s).

Frequency:
- Reproducible when heavy parallel traffic coincides with a billing/credit update. Occurred once during this customer's upgrade; support has observed similar patterns internally during large org increases but not this exact symptom.

Attempts to mitigate performed so far:
- Customer staggered worker starts (reduced concurrent workers) which reduced 429 frequency.
- Support performed a manual quota refresh for the tenant; partial improvement observed.

Attachments:
- Raw request + response examples supplied by customer (attached logs)
- Support trace IDs: trace-rw-8421, trace-rw-8422

investigation_notes: Checked billing service events: invoice and credit update accepted at 2026-03-09T23:00Z; billing write recorded to primary DB.
Rate-limiter ingestion pipeline shows a backlog for quota-refresh events at edge-fanout stage; some fanout worker retries were queued due to transient S3 metadata latency.
Edge nodes running keepalive-proxy version 2.7.1 held cached token windows that were not invalidated until TTL expiry (~9m) — caused partial stale-per-route limits.
Throttle header traces show mixed limit windows: some responses include pre-upgrade window (100r/s) while others reflect new window (1000r/s).
Hypothesis: billing->pubsub fanout occasionally stalls when org-level updates collide with high telemetry load; causes window mismatch across edge nodes until TTL refresh.
Searched for related incidents: similar pattern noted in SUP-412900 (keepalive affinity) but root cause here tied to refill event delivery path, not sticky sessions.
Impact scope estimated: affects only sessions that start within the propagation gap; established long-lived sessions pick up new tokens after reconnection or TTL expiry.
workaround: Recommended immediate steps to customer: 1) Stagger startup of bulk workers with randomized 30–90s jitter. 2) Temporarily raise per-tenant burst allowance via support console (we applied a +2x burst credit to slate-12345). 3) For streaming clients, prefer reconnect after upgrade to pick up refreshed windows.
next_steps: 1) SRE to patch fanout retry logic to avoid S3 metadata stalls (track as INT follow-up). 2) Product to evaluate reducing TTL on per-route token caches during tenant-level quota changes. 3) Add monitoring alert for refill-propagation-lag > 30s. 4) Follow up with customer once hotfix scheduled.
public_response_template: Hi <Customer>, thanks for reporting this — we identified a propagation delay between billing and our rate-limiter that can cause short windows of 429s after large org credit updates. We've applied a temporary burst increase to your account and recommend staggering worker startups while we implement a backend fix. We'll update you with a timeline for the permanent remediation.
customer_impact_notes: SlateDocs had 3 failed ingestion batches; engineering temporarily reran jobs after workaround. No data loss reported. Customer requested timeline for permanent fix and compensation consideration for failed jobs.
